title: Dispatch CSA 1: Survey Party Returns Three Days Before Departure
summary: Four names were entered on the manifest. Three people came home.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: At a quarter past seven yesterday morning, three members of the Calder Survey entered the Eidetical Institute through its front door and requested medical attention. According to the Institute’s posted schedule, their expedition into the Eidetic Stratum is not due to depart until Monday.

Professor Elian Vey, navigator Silas Rook, and instrument maker Mara Bell arrived in the clothes in which they are expected to travel. Their coats bore the green mineral dust associated with the Calder aperture. Their instruments included a survey drum bearing six days of readings. Each had suffered exposure burns to the hands. The fourth member named on the expedition manifest, junior Eidetician Ada Quill, was absent.

“Miss Quill did not come back,” Professor Vey told this newspaper. He declined to describe the circumstances, saying only that the party had crossed a region in which distances could not be trusted. The Institute has issued no notice of death and has asked the public to refrain from approaching Miss Quill or her family.

Such restraint may be difficult to observe. Miss Quill was seen this morning at her lodging on North Loom Street, and says she has never crossed the Calder aperture. “I am packing,” she told our reporter, holding the list she had made for Monday’s departure. “I should think that was proof enough.”

Institute director Dr. Cecily Marr called the returned party’s account “a matter of urgent investigation.” She would not say whether the scheduled expedition will proceed. Behind her, through the open door of the equipment room, our reporter saw a second survey drum awaiting collection. Its number matched the one brought back yesterday.
